subject.title: Session hangs indefinitely when compaction times out, causing repeated duplicate message sends

question: What should be the canonical recovery and idempotency boundary when compaction times out after a reply may already have been delivered?
rationale: Source review shows real gaps, but choosing whether to fail closed, reconcile delivered output, rotate poisoned sessions, or expose an in-product repair path changes session-state and channel-delivery semantics across several related trackers.

options.title: Choose a unified recovery contract
options.body: Keep this issue canonical while maintainers define terminal state, logical-send idempotency, already-delivered reconciliation, and non-technical recovery before splitting implementation work.

options.title: Split after partial trackers own every slice
options.body: Make https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/92043, https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/53008, and https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/96242 own the separate surfaces, then close this only after each remaining behavior is explicitly covered.

options.title: Limit core to existing mitigations
options.body: Accept current queue and compaction mitigations as the supported boundary and leave broader duplicate-send recovery to operator guidance or plugins, with the known product tradeoff documented.

recommendation.title: Choose a unified recovery contract
recommendation.body: Keep this issue canonical while maintainers define terminal state, logical-send idempotency, already-delivered reconciliation, and non-technical recovery before splitting implementation work.

likelyOwner.reason: They are the live assignee and strongest current-history owner across the compaction timeout recovery paths inspected here.
